title: Headache, visual disturbance or epigastric pain (pre-eclampsia screen)
summary: Headache, visual symptoms, epigastric/RUQ pain, or a raised blood pressure reading — screening for pre-eclampsia.
redFlags: BP ≥160/110 mmHg — admit regardless of symptoms.

Visual disturbance (flashing lights, blurring, or loss of vision), a severe headache not relieved by usual analgesia, epigastric/right-upper-quadrant pain, or persistent vomiting with headache — screen for at every contact, whatever the BP.

blocks.heading: Severe hypertension — BP ≥160/110 mmHg
bullets: Arrange immediate transfer for admission — severe hypertension requires urgent assessment and treatment regardless of symptoms.
Repeat BP measurement to confirm; do not delay referral awaiting repeat if clearly severe.
Full pre-eclampsia bloods (FBC, U&E, LFTs), urine protein:creatinine ratio, and fetal assessment (CTG, growth/Doppler as indicated) arranged on arrival.
Escalate to obstetric team immediately.
Safety-net: call 999 immediately if a seizure occurs, or if severe headache, visual loss, confusion, or feeling very unwell develop before arrival.

blocks.heading: Raised BP (140/90–159/109 mmHg) with severe symptoms present
bullets: Treat as suspected severe pre-eclampsia — arrange immediate transfer for admission.
Full pre-eclampsia bloods and fetal assessment (CTG, growth/Doppler as indicated) on arrival.
Escalate to obstetric team immediately — anticipate need for antihypertensive treatment and magnesium sulfate per local protocol if severe features confirmed.
See the Eclampsia emergency drill if any seizure activity develops.

blocks.heading: Raised BP (140/90–159/109 mmHg), no severe symptoms
bullets: Arrange same-day assessment — repeat BP, urine protein:creatinine ratio, pre-eclampsia bloods (FBC, U&E, LFTs).
Fetal assessment — CTG and consider growth/Doppler review if not recently done.
Discuss with obstetric team; consider need for antihypertensive treatment per local protocol.
Seen within 15 minutes (face-to-face) / attend within the hour (phone).

blocks.heading: Severe symptoms with normal or unknown BP
bullets: Arrange same-day assessment — pre-eclampsia symptoms warrant BP and urine protein checked even if a previous reading was normal, since pre-eclampsia can progress quickly.
Full pre-eclampsia bloods (FBC, U&E, LFTs) and fetal assessment (CTG).
Discuss with obstetric team.
Seen within 15 minutes (face-to-face) / attend within the hour (phone).

blocks.heading: Risk factors present, no red-flag symptoms
bullets: Risk factors: first pregnancy, previous pre-eclampsia, chronic hypertension, pre-existing diabetes, multiple pregnancy, BMI over 35, maternal age 40 or over, family history.
Arrange same-day BP and urinalysis given risk factor(s) present, even without severe symptoms.
Simple analgesia advice per local formulary — signpost to local guidance/BNF rather than giving medication advice directly.
Seen within 1 hour (face-to-face) / same-day assessment (phone).

blocks.heading: Simple headache, no red flags or risk factors
bullets: Reassure and advise simple measures (rest, hydration); signpost to local/BNF guidance for analgesia in pregnancy.
Advise BP check at next routine contact if not done recently.

blocks.heading: Safety-netting to give
bullets: Contact the unit again immediately if visual disturbance, epigastric pain, sudden swelling, or a severe/persistent headache develop.
Call 999 immediately if a seizure occurs at any point.

blocks.heading: What to document
bullets: BP reading(s) and time taken.
Symptoms screened for and result (positive/negative for each).
Risk factors present.
Plan for bloods/urine/fetal assessment and time of referral/admission.
